newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent may swim seasonal tide to spring rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent may swim seasonal tide to spring rally.

text.p: Prices of IPE Brent crude oil futures may strengthen in March or April in what some brokers and analysts described as a cyclical pattern ahead of the driving season.

That means the crude market, which dropped like an anchor from its high of $24.91 a barrel in January to $20.55 on Monday, a fall of 18 percent, may stay under pressure for a few more weeks before mounting a rally.
Since 1991, on a spot month continuation chart, the low for the first half of the year has always occurred in January or February -- four times in January and twice in February.
But the peak for the first half of the year was evenly spread out from March to June, and half of the time it was the high for the entire year.
Brent was not expected to retest its post-Gulf War high of $25.06, hit in October, but the chart patterns reflect seasonal fundamentals that may offer a crutch.

"It will start anywhere between February and April. Gasoline prices will slowly increase over the spring period until we get to the peak of the summer," when wholesale demand drops off because stocks are full, said Jeff Potter, managing director of brokers Univest Ireland Ltd in Dublin.
In 1996 on a weekly chart, for example, Brent crude began the year by reaching $19.31, then promptly fell to $15.93 by early February, and then soared to $23.30 in April.

The spring rally is the mirror image of a seasonal oil market rally that can occur in September and October, before the peak heating oil season when inventories are built up in anticipation of household demand, analysts said.
In the last two years, the spread between premium unleaded barges in Northwest Europe and front-month Brent rallied from lows near $1.50 a tonne in January to $6.50 and $9 by April.
Swaps on the second quarter crack spread on Tuesday edged up from $4.95 to $5.20 a barrel.
"It could still be a while before we start a slow progression upwards," Potter said. "It has a lot to do with the stockbuilding strategy by the majors and we don't know what they are."
"There's been a lot of movement of gasoline to the U.S.(from Europe) in January. Maybe they don't need to buy much for the time being," he said.
IPE Brent blend crude for March delivery rose 18 cents on Tuesday to $21.31 a barrel after hitting a fresh 5-1/2 month low yesterday.
Prices are well above their year-ago level of $15.93 -- which was the low for all of 1996.
A trader said that when heating oil demand winds down, diesel demand tends to increase from the agricultural sector and helps to put a floor under crude.

"This tends to bottom out the market in early February or early March and then rally going into June," she said. "We're telling all our heating oil buyers that the low of the fourth quarter (of the next winter season) is usually in the first quarter (before)."
Bob MacMinn, president of MPAS in Toronto, said he was telling his clients to take a close look at gasoline prices now, and their impact on the rest of the complex.
Dating to 1992, the average rise in gasoline futures between the January low and the April high has been 14.98 cents a gallon -- and the seasonality has worked all five years, he said.
"Seasonals in the gasoline market are just as strong as those for heating oil," he said. "That seasonality is typically something you don't want to stand in front of."
